gap_policy: M1/M2 decision run over 2024-10-01..2026-04-30. Three sessions the NSE calendar expects are absent from the corpus: 2024-11-20, 2025-04-30 and 2025-05-08. The decision is taken over the 385 sessions that exist. The window is NOT narrowed to avoid them: narrowing to a hole-free sub-range would either fragment one pre-registered trial into three, or discard roughly 140 sessions including the 2024-11-20 regime change the per-epoch analysis exists to look at. 2024-11-20 is itself an epoch boundary (SEBI weekly-expiry cull, contract size increase, expiry-day ELM), and losing it costs little for a reason worth stating: it was a Wednesday, and pre-Tuesday-change expiries fell on Thursdays, so no settlement is lost. The boundary merely lacks its first day's marks, which biases neither side of it. 2025-04-30 and 2025-05-08 are interior single-session holes in the intraday_position_limits_2025 regime with no structural significance.

hypothesis.mechanism: Intermediation rent. One side of the Indian index-option market persistently demands convexity — index hedgers and retail buyers of protection — and the capacity-constrained intermediaries who absorb that flow cannot lay it off. They are paid for three frictions they carry rather than for a preference they hold: inventory risk in a book they cannot fully hedge, jump exposure that no dynamic hedge replicates because the underlying gaps, and margin that binds hardest at precisely the moment the payout is owed. The premium is therefore the rent on scarce risk-bearing capacity, and it should be observable as implied variance sitting systematically above the variance subsequently realised. Selling variance collects that rent.

epochs.cross_epoch_justification:
H1'S ARGUMENT DOES NOT COVER THIS WINDOW, and stretching it would be dishonest. H1's gate
permitted one boundary — stt_rise_2026, a change in a RATE — and stated in terms that this
"does NOT justify a window crossing weekly_expiry_cull_2024 or nse_expiry_tuesday_2025.
Those changed the traded object." This window crosses both of those and three more:

  stt_rise_2024                        2024-10-01  (the window opens on it)
  weekly_expiry_cull_2024              2024-11-20  weekly expiries culled, contract size
                                                   raised, expiry-day ELM added
  calendar_spread_relief_removed_2025  2025-02-10
  intraday_position_limits_2025        2025-04-01
  nse_expiry_tuesday_2025              2025-09-01  expiry moved Thursday -> Tuesday
  stt_rise_2026                        2026-04-01

Two of those changed the traded object itself. A single pooled number over this window
describes a market that never existed, and no argument makes it describe one.

SO WHY POOL AT ALL. Because the alternative is worse, and because the pooled number is
still the answer to a question worth asking. Splitting the window into six graded
sub-windows would burn six trials against a family already carrying five, deflate every
one of the six Sharpes accordingly, hand the researcher a post-hoc choice of which regime
to believe, and leave the largest sub-window with fewer sessions than H1 already showed
were too few. The pooled verdict is the honest form of "does this premium survive being
traded through everything the regulator did to this market", which is a real question with
a real answer, and it is the question a single unconditional model can be graded on.

THE POOLED VERDICT IS THE GRADED ONE. The per-epoch breakdown below is DESCRIPTIVE and
UNGRADED. That assignment is made here, before any number exists, precisely because it is
the assignment a disappointing pooled result would most want to revisit.

What the pooled number therefore means, stated in advance: it is a statement about the
average of six regimes weighted by their session counts, and it is NOT a statement about
any one of them. If the per-epoch table shows the effect living in one regime, that is the
finding, and it is a finding this gate cannot grade.
